meeting_header:
Date: 2027-08-19 | Start: 15:30 UTC | Duration: 55m
Attendees: Nina Patel (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Evelyn Park (Redwood CSM); Liam O'Connor (Centauri Head of AI), Priya Shah (Platform Eng), Marco Ruiz (Product)
Recording: enabled | Notes: golden runbook + regression strategy kickoff
summary: Kickoff to define Centauri Retail POC success criteria and hands-on quality evaluation plan. Agreed to a "golden runbook" approach: curated golden prompts, regression playlist, hallucination/format checks, and a weighted scoring rubric. Discussed workload sizing for throughput/latency gates, timeline for benchmark runs, and security/retention constraints (KMS/SOC2). Next steps: share prompts/rubric, run baseline perf, provide dataset, schedule benchmark review.
topics: Hallucination detection rules and format validations
Workload sizing: concurrency, token budgets, expected QPS
Security: KMS, retention, SOC2, VPC concerns
transcript:
[00:00] Nina Patel: hey everyone, thanks for taking the time. quick roll call?
[00:07] Liam O'Connor: Liam here, thanks. Priya and Marco with me also.
[00:11] Priya Shah: hi all.
[00:13] Marco Ruiz: hey.
[00:15] Marcus Li: Marcus from Redwood, SE, hey, excited to dig into the eval flow.
[00:19] Evelyn Park: Evelyn, CSM, I'll be coordinating deliverables.
[00:22] Nina Patel: awesome. the goal today is to align on the POC success criteria and a practical quality eval that we can run during the four-week pilot. we'll introduce our "golden runbook" concept — it's like golden prompts + operational runbook + regression playlist.
[00:36] Liam O'Connor: that term works for us. quick context: Centauri's primary surface is chat-like product recommender for retail agents, low-latency is critical during peak — think checkout assistance. also strict data retention policies for PII.
[00:52] Nina Patel: great, helps. Marcus, can you outline the proposed golden runbook components?
[00:58] Marcus Li: sure. high level: 1) golden prompt set — 50 canonical prompts that represent key user journeys (checkout exception, returns, upsell), 2) regression playlist — ~300 cases combining golden prompts + edge cases to run after each model tweak, 3) hallucination checks — fact verification heuristics and format validation (SKUs, price formats), 4) scoring rubric — weighted metrics across correctness, format fidelity and safety.
[01:22] Marco Ruiz: on hallucination checks, can you give an example? like when the model invents inventory locations?
[01:27] Marcus Li: exact example — if prompt asks "is item XYZ in-store 108?" and model says "yes, aisle 7", we want the system to flag when an unverified factual assertion is present. we propose a two-tier check: string-level pattern checks (e.g., SKU regex, currency) and a downstream fact-check call against your inventory API for flagged items.
[01:47] Priya Shah: downstream call worries me for latency — we can't hit inventory API synchronously per token.
[01:53] Marcus Li: agreed, tradeoff. our recommended pattern for POC: run fact-checks asynchronously for the eval pipeline — they don't affect user latency for the POC. for production, options: cache, prefix KV-cache, or use a sync fast-path for only high-confidence assertions. (note: sometimes I say K-V cache or KV cache, transcription may show K-V).
[02:12] Liam O'Connor: ok that works for the evaluation. what's the scoring rubric look like?
[02:17] Nina Patel: we like a weighted score: correctness 0-5, format 0-3, hallucination penalty -0 to -5, safety filter pass/fail. final normalized 0-100. pass gate is 80+ for golden set and <5% high hallucination rate on regression playlist.
[02:33] Marco Ruiz: can you elaborate on "format"?
[02:36] Marcus Li: sure — format means output tokens match required structure: e.g., JSON object with fields {sku, availability, recommended_reason}. we'll validate using a light schema parser; failures are format errors. also measure response structure drift across model variants.
[02:52] Priya Shah: how do we handle partial matches? e.g., sku present but wrong field name?
[02:56] Marcus Li: we assign fractional points; schema mismatch lowers format score but doesn't automatically fail unless critical fields missing. we capture example outputs for manual review.
[03:07] Nina Patel: on workload sizing — Centauri said peak QPS is approx 150 requests/sec for chat during promos, average tokens per request ~250-400 with expected concurrency bursts. Marcus, what should we provision for the POC?
[03:22] Marcus Li: for a realistic benchmark we'll simulate a 10-minute sustained window at 150 QPS with 95th token length 400, plus burst test at 300 QPS for 60 seconds. For the initial run, we'll do a smaller smoke: 10k requests sample (distributed across golden and regression playlists) to get baseline latency and cost. we'll provide a runbook for hosted and dedicated variants.
[03:45] Liam O'Connor: our infra team prefers starting hosted to validate model quality before we think about dedicated.
[03:52] Nina Patel: that's common. we'll run both hosted baseline and a dedicated emulation using reserved capacity config so you can compare latency tails and unit cost.
[03:59] Priya Shah: security: we need SOC2 evidence, and if we use hosted we need to know how long Redwood retains logs, and KMS handling.
[04:08] Evelyn Park: we'll share our security package (SOC2 report, pen-test summary) and a short doc on retention. retention defaults for hosted POC are 30 days but we can arrange shorter retention and customer-managed KMS for private deployments.
[04:21] Marco Ruiz: can you do per-token cost estimate for the benchmark? rough order of magnitude so we can get budget sign-off.
[04:29] Marcus Li: yes, we'll provide a cost estimate for the sample run and the full 4-week pilot with expected traffic. quick rough: sample 10k at 300 tokens avg is X compute units — we'll include breakdown in the cost sheet.
[04:41] Liam O'Connor: timeline? four weeks is tight — what milestones do you suggest?
[04:45] Nina Patel: proposed timeline: Week 0 (this week): finalize golden prompts and dataset; Week 1: baseline runs (hosted) and initial scoring; Week 2: regression tuning + nightlies; Week 3: dedicated emulation + cost comparison; Week 4: acceptance & handoff. we can compress if Centauri can provide redacted dataset quickly.
[05:03] Priya Shah: we can get the redacted set within 48 hours, but legal needs to sign the DPA first.
[05:09] Evelyn Park: I'll follow-up with DPA and legal contacts — timeline contingent on DPA signature, but we'll treat dataset prep as parallel work.
[05:18] Marco Ruiz: about the regression playlist frequency — do you recommend nightly runs or on deploy?
[05:23] Marcus Li: both. nightly regression for continuous quality, and full playlist run on model swap or config change. for POC we'll run nightly against a curated subset and full playlist weekly because of cost.
[05:34] Liam O'Connor: what's the tooling for scoring? can we integrate in our CI?
[05:38] Marcus Li: yes we provide a CSV/JSON exporter and a small CLI to run the scoring locally or in your CI. outputs include per-case scores, hallucination flags, and example deltas. we'll link the repo.
[05:49] Nina Patel: ok let's capture acceptance criteria: 1) golden set average >= 80% normalized score, 2) regression playlist has <5% high hallucination flags, 3) 95th latency under your target 400ms in dedicated emulation (or agreed SLA), 4) security signoffs completed. agree?
[06:05] Liam O'Connor: yes with caveat on latency — our 95th target is 350ms for user-facing flows.
[06:11] Marcus Li: noted — we'll push the emulation to try hit 350ms 95th in dedicated config; hosted may be higher.
[06:19] Priya Shah: will you share the golden prompts in a format we can edit?
[06:23] Nina Patel: yes, we'll share a google sheet + JSON export. link will be in follow up.
[06:27] Marco Ruiz: what about false positives in hallucination detection? we don't want too many false hits.
[06:31] Marcus Li: agree — we tune thresholds and use a human-in-the-loop sample for the first 500 flags to calibrate. we can also add a severity score so only high-severity flags count against the pass gate.
[06:43] Liam O'Connor: on regression cases, any guidance on how many must be automated vs manual review?
[06:48] Marcus Li: automatable checks for format and regex/fact checks — maybe 70% automatable. remaining 30% are subjective recommendations and require manual QA. we'll provide a review UI export for triage.
[06:59] Nina Patel: any other concerns from Centauri?
[07:02] Priya Shah: just two — KMS for hosted and data locality (we need EU region for some customers).
[07:07] Evelyn Park: KMS customer-managed and EU region hosting are optioned for Private deployment; for the hosted POC we can specify EU tenancy if you need.
[07:16] Liam O'Connor: good to hear. one more: can the scoring include business KPIs like conversion lift predicted?
[07:22] Marcus Li: we can add a correlation analysis to map model outputs to downstream KPI proxies using a sample of past events. that's an optional deep-dive during Week 3 if you want.
[07:32] Nina Patel: wrap-up / next steps check: 1) Nina share golden prompts & scoring template by Monday. 2) Liam to upload dataset + retention policy (or at least a pointer) by Saturday. 3) Marcus run hosted baseline with 10k sample and share logs by next Thursday. 4) Evelyn to send DPA and schedule follow-up benchmark review.
[07:50] Liam O'Connor: that's fine.
[07:52] Priya Shah: yep.
[07:53] Marco Ruiz: ok, thanks all.
[07:55] Marcus Li: thanks.
[07:56] Nina Patel: thanks, we'll follow up with links and the runbook. meeting adjourned.
[08:00] (recording end)

Notes: transcript includes minor transcription artifacts; references to KV cache may appear as K-V cache. Shared artifacts referenced: "golden-prompts-v1.csv" (link), "redwood-scoring-rubric.xlsx" (link), perf-runbook.md (link).
